title: Шеф берёт заказ на себя  (The Chef Takes Over the Order)

segments.t: Moments later, the waiter returns with the plate untouched: the sheikh did not like Senya and Fedya's creation. As the two cooks bicker and blame each other, Chef Barinov steps in to cook the dish himself.
Поверни меня к нему, я в него плюну.
Слушай, сейчас шеф получит наш перстень.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'For some reason the sheikh did not like it.' The grammar packs 'for some reason' and 'pleased' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'He did not like your impudent smile.' Notice how Russian puts 'smile' and 'pleased' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'Take a look at your own face.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'look'. Fedya answers right away.
Поверни меня к нему, я в него плюну.
'Turn me toward him, I will spit at him.' The meaning hinges on 'turn' working together with 'will spit' in spoken Russian.
'Thank you, taste it yourself.' In Russian, the idea of 'thank you' flows naturally into 'yourself' without extra filler words.
'There is nothing to taste here, got it?' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'here', while 'understood' completes the thought. Senya answers right away.
'Let us make it one more time.' Notice how Russian expresses 'let's' and 'time' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Do you want to taste some more?' The meaning hinges on 'else' working together with 'to taste' in spoken Russian.
'Today is your day off.' The grammar packs 'tonight' and 'day off' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I will make everything myself.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'I', while 'will do' completes the thought.
'Lyova, bring the cheese and the pear.' The grammar packs 'Lyova' and 'pear' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Слушай, сейчас шеф получит наш перстень.

'Listen, now the Chef will get our ring.' The meaning hinges on 'listen' working together with 'signet' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Поверни меня к нему, я в него плюну.
Слушай, сейчас шеф получит наш перстень.
Pushing his bungling cooks aside, Barinov prepares the baked pear with blue cheese himself and heads upstairs to deliver it in person. See you next time!
